samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both use beekeeping words throughout (hive, queen, brood, frames, honey stores, varroa). B fits the keeper's dozen hives better: a grid of Hive 1–12 that each read 'Never opened' tells them where to start. Its temperament buttons are small, though, and 'Never opened' is a bit misleading for hives that have been opened but not yet logged. A has larger, cleaner tap targets. Neither screenshot shows the empty log or the save confirmation, so items 2 and 3 are partly inferred. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages label everything in beekeeping terms (queen, brood, frames, honey stores, pests). B has larger radio and checkbox tap targets and fewer fiddly inputs, which suits someone standing at a hive. A's small 1–5 temperament buttons and extra weather fields work less well there, though A's twelve-hive 'Never opened' grid is a useful first-run cue. Neither screenshot shows the empty log or the save confirmation, so items 2 and 3 are only partly visible.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B fits the keeper better: it uses beekeeping groups like 'Queen & brood', queen-cell types and brood pattern, shows the twelve hives at a glance, and uses large chip buttons with a preselected hive, which suits use at the hive. A has the clearer empty log message ('No inspections logged yet… press Save inspection') and plain checkboxes. B's actual log empty state isn't visible, and it assumes hives are numbered 1–12. Neither screenshot shows the confirmation after saving. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use beekeeping words throughout: hive, queen cells, capped brood, frames of brood, stores of honey. B's empty log explains what the area is for and says to fill in the form after opening a hive and press Save. In A's screenshot the log area isn't visible; the only empty-state cue is 'never opened' on each hive tile. A's pill-style buttons are easier to tap than B's checkboxes, but neither screenshot shows a save confirmation, and neither invents specifics or adds features beyond the log.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both forms use strong beekeeping vocabulary (queen, eggs/larvae, brood pattern, stores, varroa), but A's chips and inputs are noticeably larger tap targets and its form is leaner. B adds a weather field whose placeholder includes a specific temperature figure, and its smaller chips suit a gloved keeper at the hive less well. Neither screenshot shows the empty log state or the save confirmation, so those items are scored conservatively. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages use real beekeeping words (hive, queen, brood pattern, eggs/larvae, stores, varroa, hive beetles). B has larger, better-spaced pill buttons, marks optional fields clearly and adds useful hive-side choices like queen cells and swarm cells, so it suits a keeper at the hive better. Neither screenshot shows the empty log area or the confirmation after saving, so items 2 and 3 can only be judged in part; A's weather field is a plain text box with an 'e.g.' placeholder, not a widget or a made-up fact.

samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A puts lending (member, then tools, then a single lend button) and returning (scan a tag or click Return) side by side, which fits a busy front desk well. However, it mixes 'borrowing/borrower' with 'member', and its 'Loan length: 1 week' looks like an invented policy: it can be changed but isn't labeled as a default. B uses one tool-first list with clear status chips and a 'Pick a tool' prompt, but it starts lending from the tool instead of the member, also uses 'borrower', and its 'Held back' repair status and 'Details' button drift toward inventory management; neither screenshot shows the error messages. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A keeps lending and taking back on one tool list with a clear prompt in the side panel, and it doesn't invent a loan length. Its search label mixes in 'borrower', and lending starts from a tool rather than from a member. B has a strong flow that starts from the member, plus a quick return by tag, but its 'Loan length: 1 week' looks like policy and isn't labeled as a default, and it mixes borrower, loan, lend and return. The screenshots show neither answer's messages for a member not found or a tool already out.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B puts lending and returning side by side with one-click Take back, and its due-back date is a normal date field labeled as a one-week default you can change, which fits item 4 well. A has a stronger member-lookup flow with tabs, but it offers 3/7/14-day loan lengths without saying they are defaults. That reads as an invented policy, and A also mixes 'borrower' and 'member'. Neither screenshot shows the edge-case messages, and B's free-text borrower field gives no clear member-not-found path. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B has a real member lookup (name or phone, showing what each member has out and any overdue tools), a numbered lend flow and a separate take-back tab, so it covers the whole 'find a member, then finish a lend or return' flow better. A's member field is plain text with no lookup, so there is no 'member not found' case, and it mixes 'Borrower' with 'member'. A handles policy better, though: its due-back date is clearly labeled as a default and can be changed, while B's 3/7/14-day loan options look like made-up loan lengths, and B also mixes terms (borrowing, free, late).

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A is a clean two-step desk flow with consistent wording (member, tool, lend, take back) and plain availability states, and it shows no invented policy. B also works and shows more useful context, such as who has each tool, but it adds an inventory-totals header and preset 3/7/14-day loan lengths with 7 days preselected and not labeled as a default, which goes against rubric items 4 and 5. Error-state messages can't be checked fully from either static screenshot. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B is a focused desk screen. It has clear lend and take-back modes, a sticky action bar that says what is still needed, and specific tool states (on the shelf, not available with its date, needs repair), and it invents no policies. Answer A shows inventory totals as fact in the header and uses a preselected 7-day loan length that isn't labeled as a default. It also mixes wording ('lending ticket', 'loan length', 'borrowing'). Both screens look able to finish a lend, but the screenshots can't show whether either has a member-not-found message or what happens after a lend or return.
